title: FRUC: Feedforward Dynamic Scene Reconstruction from Uncalibrated Collaborative Driving Views
claim: Aggregating sparse uncalibrated views from other agents in one feedforward pass fills blind spots and enables downstream scene editing and view synthesis.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: input views, central reconstruction, what-if outputs
description: A wide three-part figure. On the left, two tinted boxes hold street-view image pairs: an orange 'Collab View' and a purple 'Ego View'. A dashed blue box between them reads 'Sparse and Dynamic Cross-Agent View Correlation'. In the center, a top-down road schematic shows an ego red car, a collaborator yellow car, and a gray 'Ego Blind' zone. Beside it is a large rendered 3D Gaussian scene with camera icons for Ego and Collab. Two ellipses compare 'Only Ego View' (green, blurry) against 'FRUC' (red, sharper) at the blind spot, labeled 'Blindspot Completion'. Yellow arrows read 'Feedforward Reconstruction' and 'What-if Analysis'. On the right, a green panel shows 'Future Action Rehearsal' with three shifted novel views. An orange panel shows 'Current Status Analysis', which splits the ego view into static and dynamic objects.
caption: Collaborative driving scene reconstruction and what-if analysis with FRUC. By aggregating uncalibrated, sparse, and dynamic cross-agent observations, FRUC seamlessly completes the ego vehicle's blind spots via a single feedforward pass. It provides accurate occluded background recovery, leading to reliable scene editing and high-fidelity novel view synthesis.
abstract: We present FRUC, a feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for dynamic scene reconstruction from uncalibrated collaborative driving views. Existing multi-agent reconstruction frameworks are often hindered by rigid prerequisites, demanding precise spatial calibration and slow per-scene optimization. In this paper, we rethink this task by conceptualizing a distributed multi-vehicle network as a spatio-temporally unstructured ego-centric multi-camera system, where the core challenge lies in enhancing ego-centric occluded geometry through collaboration without degrading the ego's accurately observed visible geometry, while preserving reconstruction efficiency. For efficient reconstruction, FRUC is built upon a visual grounded geometric Transformer backbone to enable one-shot, calibration-free inference from a flexible number of multi-vehicle views. To achieve non-destructive geometric supplementation under uncalibrated cross-agent misalignment, FRUC first introduces an ego-centric causal occlusion field that explicitly derives occlusion evolution as latent priors by modeling agent-wise spatio-temporal correlations. Guided by these occlusion priors, it further formulates cross-agent integration as a deterministic residual denoising process via zero-initialized injection, turning challenging cross-agent fusion into bounded residual learning for robust collaborative blind-spot completion. Through extensive evaluations on real-world V2X-Real and UrbanIng-V2X datasets, FRUC is shown to be a new state-of-the-art for the scene reconstruction of dynamic collaborative driving environments, significantly outperforming existing methods in both rendering quality and efficiency. Code is available at https://github.com/yihangtao/FRUC.git.
